title: How to Change a Toilet | This Old House (Toilet Replacement Tutorial)
summary: This video from This Old House presents a practical, step‑by‑step toilet replacement focused on basic hands‑on technique and safety. The host demonstrates shutting off the water, draining the tank and bowl, disconnecting lines, removing the toilet, inspecting and securing the flange, installing a new seal (wax ring) with a thicker option and horn, seating the toilet onto the flange, trimming and capping the closet bolts, reconnecting the water supply, and testing the installation. The recording emphasizes common pitfalls (like over-tightening one side, damaging the porcelain, or leaving standing water) and uses simple tools (primarily a wrench and basic cutting tools) to illustrate a standard replacement workflow suitable for DIY homeowners.
topics: wax ring vs thicker wax seal with horn

sections.title: Intro and approach
sections.description: Host introduces a basic toilet replacement and suggests that, in many cases, a single adjustable wrench or pliers may suffice to break connections.

sections.title: Shutoff and initial drainage
sections.description: Shut off the cold water supply by turning the shutoff clockwise, then prepare to drain the tank; the tank is flushed to begin emptying into the bowl.

sections.title: Removing remaining moisture
sections.description: After flushing, use a small cup, sponge, or turkey baster to remove remaining water from the tank and the bowl to ensure the system is mostly dry before further disassembly.

sections.title: Disconnections and removing the toilet
sections.description: Loosen and remove the cold water supply line, then disconnect and remove the closet bolts. Lift the toilet off the flange and set it aside on a protective surface.

sections.title: Flange and bottom condition check
sections.description: Inspect the wax build-up and the bottom surface for the new installation; note that wax is visible and discuss placing the toilet on a protective layer while inspecting the flange area and ensuring the flange is properly attached to the subfloor.

sections.title: Wax seal, bolts, and seating
sections.description: Demonstrates selecting a thicker wax ring with a horn to direct water away from the top connection, positioning the ring, and lowering the toilet straight down onto the wax seal while applying weight for a tight seating. Then, install bolt caps and washers, and advance nuts evenly to seat onto the wax without over-tightening.

sections.title: Bolt height and finishing touches
sections.description: The stand‑off bolts are typically taller than needed; they are trimmed after seating. The bolt caps are snapped on, a bronze washer is placed, and the nuts are tightened evenly to avoid cracking the toilet.

sections.title: Reconnect water and test
sections.description: Reattach the water supply, restore water, and observe the tank filling. The host highlights the wax seal as a potential leak point if a toilet was replaced or if the wax seal failed previously.

featured_techniques.technique: Shut off water supply at the sight of the valve
Drain tank and flush to drain water into the bowl
Remove remaining water with sponge/turkey baster (not the Thanksgiving one)
Remove closet bolts and lift toilet straight up
Inspect and prepare flange mounting; secure flange to subfloor
Install thicker wax ring with horn for proper alignment
Seat toilet onto wax ring with even pressure; ensure proper seating
Install bolt caps and washers; tighten nuts evenly
Trim excess bolt length for proper height
Reconnect water supply and test fill
